summary: This note is the API reference page for the Java class java.util.Observable from the Java Platform Standard Edition 7 documentation. It explains that Observable represents an observable object in the model-view paradigm, whose observers are notified via their update method after a change. The page lists the class's constructor and methods, such as addObserver, deleteObserver, notifyObservers, setChanged, clearChanged and hasChanged, along with their behavior.
one_line: Oracle's Java SE 7 API reference page for the java.util.Observable class and its observer-notification methods.
key_facts: The Observable class is in the java.util package and was introduced in JDK1.0.
Observable represents an observable object, or "data" in the model-view paradigm.
An observer may be any object that implements the Observer interface.
After an observable instance changes, calling notifyObservers causes all observers to be notified by a call to their update method.
The order in which notifications are delivered is unspecified; the default implementation notifies observers in the order they registered interest.
The notification mechanism has nothing to do with threads and is completely separate from the wait and notify mechanism of class Object.
When an observable object is newly created, its set of observers is empty.
Two observers are considered the same if and only if the equals method returns true for them.
The public constructor Observable() constructs an Observable with zero Observers.
addObserver throws a NullPointerException if the parameter o is null.
deleteObserver called with null has no effect.
setChanged is protected and marks the object as changed so that hasChanged returns true.
clearChanged is protected, is called automatically by the notifyObservers methods, and makes hasChanged return false.
countObservers returns the number of observers of this Observable object.
